issue.title: SerializedDAG.partial_subset modifies the original DAG when it contains a mapped TaskGroup (ReferenceError with nested TaskGroups)
issue.body:
### Under which category would you file this issue?

Airflow Core

### Apache Airflow version

3.3.2

### What happened and how to reproduce it?


In `SerializedDAG.partial_subset()` (https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/airflow-core/src/airflow/serialization/definitions/dag.py#L356-L385), `filter_task_group()` shallow-copies each task group and then deep-copies the attributes listed in `type(group).__slots__`:

```python
copied = copy.copy(group)
...
for attr in type(group).__slots__:
    value = getattr(group, attr)
    value = copy.deepcopy(value, memo)
    object.__setattr__(copied, attr, value)
```

On 3.3.2:

```text
SerializedTaskGroup.__slots__       = ('_group_id', 'group_display_name', 'prefix_group_id', 'parent_group', 'dag', 'tooltip', 'doc_md', 'default_args', 'ui_color', 'ui_fgcolor', 'children', 'upstream_group_ids', 'downstream_group_ids', 'upstream_task_ids', 'downstream_task_ids')
SerializedMappedTaskGroup.__slots__ = ('_expand_input',)
```

For a `SerializedMappedTaskGroup`, `children` is not in `type(group).__slots__`, so the copy keeps the original `children` dict (`copied.children is group.children` is `True` for the mapped group and `False` for the root group and the nested `SerializedTaskGroup`). `filter_task_group()` then assigns the subset's tasks and copied child groups into that dict, so after one call the original DAG's mapped group contains the subset's task objects and the subset's copy of the nested group.

Behaviour after one `partial_subset()` call + `gc.collect()` on 3.3.2:

| DAG shape | Original DAG modified | Original tasks with dead `task_group` weakref |
|---|---|---|
| mapped group containing a nested group | yes | tasks of the nested group |
| mapped group, no nested group | yes | none |
| unmapped group containing a nested group | no | none |

Reproduction (no database needed):

```python
import gc
import tracemalloc

from airflow.sdk import DAG, task, task_group
from airflow.serialization.serialized_objects import DagSerialization


@task
def files():
    return [1, 2]


@task
def prepare(x):
    return x


@task
def convert(x):
    return x


@task_group
def inner(x):
    a = convert.override(task_id='a')(x)
    b = convert.override(task_id='b')(a)
    return b


@task
def select(x):
    return x


@task_group
def outer(x):
    p = prepare(x)
    c = convert(p)
    i = inner(c)
    return select(i)


with DAG('repro') as dag:
    outer.expand(x=files())

sdag = DagSerialization.from_dict(DagSerialization.to_dict(dag))

tracemalloc.start()
gc.collect()
base = tracemalloc.get_traced_memory()[0]
for i in range(1, 201):
    sub = sdag.partial_subset(
        task_ids=['outer.prepare'], include_downstream=True, include_upstream=False
    )
    del sub
    if i in (1, 2, 5, 50, 200):
        gc.collect()
        cur = tracemalloc.get_traced_memory()[0]
        inner_group = sdag.task_group.children['outer'].children.get('outer.inner')
        try:
            tg = sdag.task_dict['outer.inner.a'].task_group.group_id
        except ReferenceError as e:
            tg = f'ReferenceError: {e}'
        print(
            f'iter={i} mem_delta={(cur - base) / 1024:.0f}KiB '
            f'inner_id={id(inner_group):x} task_group(a)={tg}'
        )

sdag.task_group.topological_sort()
print('topological_sort ok')
```

Output on 3.3.2 (Python 3.11; ids and KiB values vary between runs):

```text
iter=1 mem_delta=23KiB inner_id=70952194a410 task_group(a)=ReferenceError: weakly-referenced object no longer exists
iter=2 mem_delta=61KiB inner_id=709521948890 task_group(a)=ReferenceError: weakly-referenced object no longer exists
iter=5 mem_delta=132KiB inner_id=7095219a8ec0 task_group(a)=ReferenceError: weakly-referenced object no longer exists
iter=50 mem_delta=937KiB inner_id=7095217bd650 task_group(a)=ReferenceError: weakly-referenced object no longer exists
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/tmp/issue_exact.py", line 52, in <module>
    sub = sdag.partial_subset(
  File ".../airflow/serialization/definitions/dag.py", line 382, in partial_subset
    object.__setattr__(dag, "task_group", filter_task_group(self.task_group, None))
  File ".../airflow/serialization/definitions/dag.py", line 374, in filter_task_group
    filtered_child = filter_task_group(child, proxy)
  File ".../airflow/serialization/definitions/dag.py", line 374, in filter_task_group
    filtered_child = filter_task_group(child, proxy)
  File ".../airflow/serialization/definitions/dag.py", line 363, in filter_task_group
    value = copy.deepcopy(value, memo)
  [... repeated copy.deepcopy frames ...]
  File ".../attr/_make.py", line 1034, in slots_getstate
    return {name: getattr(self, name) for name in state_attr_names}
RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded
```

The `outer.inner` group object in the original `sdag` is a different object at each sampled iteration (`inner_id`).

The Grid code path produces the same `ReferenceError` after a single `partial_subset()` call (same `sdag` construction as above):

```python
import gc
from airflow.api_fastapi.core_api.services.ui.grid import _find_aggregates

list(_find_aggregates(node=sdag.task_group, parent_node=None, ti_details={}))  # ok (8 nodes)
sdag.partial_subset(task_ids=['outer.prepare'], include_downstream=True, include_upstream=False)
gc.collect()
list(_find_aggregates(node=sdag.task_group, parent_node=None, ti_details={}))  # ReferenceError
```

```text
  File ".../airflow/api_fastapi/core_api/services/ui/grid.py", line 178, in _find_aggregates
  File ".../airflow/api_fastapi/core_api/services/ui/task_group.py", line 40, in <lambda>
  File ".../airflow/serialization/definitions/taskgroup.py", line 257, in topological_sort
  File ".../airflow/serialization/definitions/taskgroup.py", line 291, in _project_child_deps
    anc_idx = id_to_idx.get(tg.node_id)
ReferenceError: weakly-referenced object no longer exists
```

In 3.3.2, `partial_subset()` is called by the API server in `POST .../clearTaskInstances` (`routes/public/task_instances.py`), `routes/ui/grid.py` (when `root` is given) and `routes/ui/structure.py`.

### What you think should happen instead?


`partial_subset()` should not modify the DAG it is called on.

Replacing the loop with one that includes inherited attrs fields:

```python
for attr in (field.name for field in attrs.fields(type(group))):
```

gives, for the same script on 3.3.2 (and the `_find_aggregates` walk still returns 8 nodes after 200 `partial_subset()` calls):

```text

iter=200 mem_delta=28KiB inner_id=7841eb5c0260 task_group(a)=outer.inner
topological_sort ok
```

After applying this change to our 3.3.2 deployment, the `ReferenceError` no longer appears in the API server logs.

comments.body: Hi @jgoedeke, I'd like to work on this issue. I've looked through the `partial_subset()` behavior and the `SerializedMappedTaskGroup` inheritance/slots issue described here. I'd like to add a regression test for the shared `children` state and implement the fix using the attrs fields so inherited attributes are copied as well. Could you assign this issue to me?

@aryan9948 a PR is very welcome! Issues are usually not assigned anymore, see [Assignment Policy](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/contributing-docs/04_how_to_contribute.rst#contribute-code-changes)
